JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 14.05.2023 at about 11.00 p.m., the petitioner was riding his Bullet bike bearing Reg.No.UP- 92/AA-7934 on Vydehi Hospital road and when he reached near KTPO Junction, Bangalore, at that time, the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51/MN-1447 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's Bullet bike, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Manipal Hospital,
wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and undergone surgery.

So far, the petitioner has spent more than Rs.25,00,000/- towards medical expenses,
nourishment and conveyance.
Further he required another 5 to 10 lakhs towards future surgeries, since he has to undergo few more surgeries in future.
3. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
He is aged about 26 years.

He obtained the offer letter from siemens EDA in Private Limited and obtained offer package of Rs.36,00,000/-
per annum.

Due to the permanent disability, the petitioner has suffered pain and sufferings,
permanent disability, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.

4. The respondent no.1/ the RC owner of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51/MN-1447 has filed written statement and contended that the claim petition is not maintainable and is barred by limitation and that the said car has been falsely implicated in the alleged accident and that the said car was not at all involved in the accident.

5. Respondent no.2 /the insurer of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51/MN-1447 has filed written statement and contended that the claim petition is barred by limitation and that there is 7 days delay in lodging the complaint and that in the police complaint, FIR, Panchanama and sketch the registration number of the alleged offending vehicle is not mentioned.
In the police complaint and FIR, it is just mentioned "four wheeler vehicle, registration number unknown".

The respondent no.2 further contended that the motorcycle bearing No.UP-92- AA-7934 was not having policy to cover the risk of rider of motorcycle, a false case is filed against the driver of Car bearing No.KA-51-MN-1447 to get compensation and that as per the IMV report, the registration number of the car mentioned as KA-51-MS-1447 and that Car bearing No.KA-51-MN-1447 was not at all involved in the accident and that the alleged accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent Saswat Khuntia vs Manjunath on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30676209/
2 riding on the part of the rider of the motorcycle, but to get compensation petitioner, the police filed the charge sheet against the driver of Car bearing No.KA-51-MN-1447 as accused no.1 and against the rider/petitioner of the motorcycle as Accused No.2 and that as per the IMV report, the car not sustained any damages.

sentences.text:
The respondent no.2 further contended that the driver of the insured vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence and the said vehicle was not having RC,
FC and valid permit at the time of accident.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained injuries on account of road traffic accident on 14-05-2023 at about 11-00 pm, near Vydehi Hospital road, near KTPO Junction, Bangalore, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-M-1447?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.

What Order or Award?
7.
The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and one witness as P.W.2 and marked documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P20.
The respondent no.2 has examined its Deputy Manger as Rw.1 and marked documents as Ex.R1 and R2.
8. Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and respondents and perused the entire materials placed on record.

9. My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative. Issue No.3:
As per final order, for the following;
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:-

In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 14.05.2023 at about 11.00 p.m., when the petitioner was riding his Bullet bike bearing Reg.No.UP-92/AA-7934 on Vydehi Hospital road and when he reached near KTPO Junction,
Bangalore, at that time, the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51/MN- 1447 (hereinafter referred to as the offending the vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's Bullet bike, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

sentences.text:
In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to Ex.P10 which are the police records such as F.I.R with complaint, Mahazar, sketch,
statement of witnesses notice u/Sec. 133 of IMV Act and reply given there on, IMV reports,
statement of the accused, charge sheet, order sheet in CC No. 33044/2023, wound certificate, etc.
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Debendra Chandra Khuntia, case has been registered against the driver of Unknown 4 wheeler in Crime No.0059/2023 of Mahadavapura Traffic Police Station for the offence punishable under section 283, 337 of IPC and U/sec.134(a&b), 187 of MV Act.

After completion of investigation, the investigating officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MN- 1447 as accused no.1 and against the rider/petitioner of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.UP-92-AA-7934 for the offence punishable under Section under section 283, 338 of IPC and and U/sec.134(a&b), 187 of MV Act.
13.

As observed supra the respondent no.2 has seriously disputed the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident on the ground that there is delay of 7 days in lodging the complaint and that in the medical records the history is mentioned as " fall from two wheeler" and as per IMV report no damage was caused to the offending vehicle.
14. So for as delay in lodging the complaint is concerned it is true that the accident in question was occurred on 14.05.023 and complaint came to be lodged on 20.05.2023.
In the complaint and in the FIR reason for delay has been explained.
Admittedly petitioner is the native of Odisa.
On employment he came down to Bangalore.
All the family members of the petitioner are residing at Odisa.
After the accident the father of th petitioner who is a Government employee came down to Bangalore to take care of the petitioner.

Hence it is quit natural that when complainant is stranger to Bangalore and when there is no one in Bangalore to take care of the petitioner, under Such circumstances the presence of the complainant being the father of the petitioner is required in the hospital.

If the medical records are perused, soon after the accident the petitioner was shifted to the Manipal Hospital wherein MLC was registered and police intimation was sent, to the jurisdictional police station which is evident from Ex.P18 and 19.

When police intimation was sent it is the duty of the Jurisdictional PS to visit the hospital and to record the statement of the injured, if injured was in a position to give statement or else the statement of the attendant.
Hence for the fault of the jurisdictional police the petitioner canot be blamed.

In a judgment given in MFA No.399/2012 (MV)
between united India Insurance Company Ltd VS Smt. SK Saroja and Another decided on 21.06.2019 by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.

entities.text:
MFA No.399/2012 (MV)
between united India Insurance Company Ltd VS Smt. SK Saroja and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the said case the respondent no.2 i.e.,
insurer strenuously contended that there is delay of 4 months 7 days in lodging the complaint.
In the said case though injured was admitted in the hospital but no information was given by the doctor to the police.
It was held "because the hospital authorities have committed mistake by not sending MLC report to the police, the claimant should not be made to suffer".
In the said case the driver of the insured vehicle has not appeared before the court and led any evidence to show that there was no accident caused by him.

Hence it was observed "merely because there was delay in lodging the complaint, the veracity of the complaint cannot be taken away especially for granting compensation for the injuries sustained by the complainant in the road traffic accident".

Saswat Khuntia vs Manjunath on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30676209/
4 15.

sentences.text: In the light of the observation made in the aforesaid judgment coupled with the fact that MLC was registered and MLC report was given to the jurisdictional police and the fact that petitioner is the resident of Odisa and petitioner has sustained grievous and injury and was in the hospital from the date of accident till 24.05.2023, it can be said that the petitioner has assigned valid reason for delay in lodging the complaint.
Hence the delay of 7 days in lodging the complaint will not go to the root of the case of the complainant.

16. So far as the argument canvased by the respondent no.2 denying the very involvement of offending vehicle is concerned, it is true that in the Ex.P11, 18 and 19, the history in brief is mentioned as "RTA fall from two wheeler sustained injuries to face, head and right eye.
But no where it is stated that the petitioner sustained injury due to self fall.
Even when offending vehicle hit to the motor cycle result of which petitioner fell down would amount to fall from the motor cycle.
As per the medical records, after the accident petitioner was in semi conscious state of mind.
He was not in a position to give statement.
One Pooja who accompanied the injured to the hospital has given the history of accident as "fall" .

Though the respondent no.2 has disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident on the ground that no damage was caused to the offending vehicle,
but the official of respondent no.2 company who was examined as RW.1 in her cross examination has admitted the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident and admitted that in the medical records it is mentioned that the injured was in semi conscious mind and that the injured was shifted to the hospital by one Pooja and that the driver of offending vehicle by admitting his guilty had deposited the fine amount before the jurisdictional magistrate.
When RW.1 herself has admitted the involvement of offending vehicle, there is no reason to disbelieve the version of the petitioner regarding the offending vehicle involved in the accident.

If the confessional statement of the accused at Ex.P7 is perused wherein he has admitted that due to the accident, damage was caused to the front and rear side of the car and he got it repaired from Sundaram Benz Service Center.
As observed supra the accident in question has occurred on 14.05.2023.
The driver of the offending vehicle has given confessional statement on 21.07.2023.
The vehicle was inspected through RTO on 23.06.2023.
Hence within a period of 1 month and 9 days from the date of accident the possibility of repairing the damage caused to the offending vehicle cannot be ruled out.
Though the respondent no.2 has disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident but they have not questioned the charge sheet.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 that since respondent no.2 is not a party to the charge sheet, they cannot question the charge sheet.

17. So far as the above line of argument canvased by the learned counsel for respondent no.2, it is opt to refer here the judgment relied by the learned counsel for petitioner rendered in MFA no.7493/2007 (MV) between Bajaj Allianze General Insurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Lakshmamma and others decided on 25.09.2007 wherein also the Insurance Company raised objection regarding the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.

entities.text: Bajaj Allianze General Insurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Lakshmamma and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case the owner of the vehicle did not contest the case.
Admittedly charge sheet was filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.
The owner has not denied the accident.

It was held "if really the vehicle was not involved, if a false case has been lodged and if the owner has colluded with the claimants, it was for the insurance company to challenge the same to quash the charge sheet and to direct the police to investigate properly and file an appropriate case for having lodged a false case, when there was no accident and vehicle in question had not been involved.

sentences.text:
In the said case it was held, "the charge sheet is conclusive proof and it is a summary trail the charge sheet is not challenged by the insurer or the owner of the offending vehicle, under such circumstances the claim of the claimants needs to be accepted".
19.

In Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25092 of 204) between Suhagrani and others Vs Manager Cholamandalam Ms General Insurance Company,
it was observed by referring to the facts of the said case that "
the fact that the jurisdictional police had conducted investigation and recorded the statement of various persons during course of investigation had resulted in filing of the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle".
20.

entities.text: Suhagrani and others Vs Manager Cholamandalam Ms General Insurance Company
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the observation made in the aforesaid judgment coupled with the admission of the Rw.1 would sufficient to hold that offending vehicle was involved in the accident.
21. It is not in dispute that charge sheet was filed both against the petitioner and the driver of the offending vehicle.
Admittedly the petitioner and driver of the offending vehicle have admitted their guilty before the jurisdictional magistrate and deposited the fine amount.

If the charge sheet is perused, at the time of accident the offending vehicle came from Vaidehi hospital towards Grafite India Juction in a rash and negligent manner and without giving any indication all of a sudden took the vehicle towards KTPO by taking right turn and hit to the vehicle of the petitioner which was proceeding from Grafite India Junction towards Vaidehi hospital.
If the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, the petitioner was proceeding in the straight road and the offending vehicle by taking right U turn hit to the motor cycle of the petitioner.
The petitioner was proceeding on the correct line.
Hence the offending vehicle while taking U turn and while entering the main door ought to have taken all care and caution.
Because there is allegation against the petitioner that he has ridden his vehicle in a high speed, the negligence is attributed to the petitioner and the offending vehicle at the ratio of 10:90.
Hence the petitioner has to forgo compensation to an extent of 10%.
Accordingly issue No.1 is answered in partly affirmative.
22. Issue No.2:- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.

As per the medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and Discharge summary which are marked at Ex.P10 and P11, the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient at Manipal Hospitals, Bangalore from 15-05-2023 to 24-05- 2023 for a period of 10 days.
As per the wound certificate the petitioner has sustained 10 injuries of which injury no.1 to 4 are grievous in nature and injury no.5 to 10 are simple in nature.
23. Siddappa Kare Gowda -Medical Record Officer is examined as PW.2 and through him police intimation, Accident register and Outpatient and Inpatient file are marked as Ex.P18 to Ex.P20.

Saswat Khuntia vs Manjunath on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30676209/
6 24.

entities.text: Saswat Khuntia vs Manjunath on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken, this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
25. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained 4 grievous injuries.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.80,000/- towards pain and suffering.
26. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, the petitioner has produced 23 medical bills for Rs.11,07,579/- at Ex.P.13.

As per the discharge summary the petitioner is diagnosed for Scaphoid fracture (Complete fracture of waist) with Lunate dislocation with unstable midcarpal joint right wrist + communited displaced radial head fracture.
None of the medical documents discloses any injury caused to the mouth of the petitioner and fall of any teeth.
The petitioner has filed the summary of medical bills total amounting to Rs.11,07,579/-.
Serial No.1 in Ex.P13 is the final inpatient bill for Rs. 9,41,999/-.

Serial No. 3 to 5 are the bills for Rs.51,600/-
dated 03.06.2023, bill for Rs.66,780/- dated 09.12.2023 and Rs.12,180/- dated 11.11.2023.
The said bills are pertaining to the treatment taken in Dental Medicine MHW.
As per the said document tooth implantation was made.
When the petitioner has not sustained any injury on mouth and no tooth was lost due to the accident, the question of tooth implantation does not arise.
Hence it can be said that bill amount of Rs.51,600, Rs. 66,780/- and Rs.12,180/- are not relating to the accidental injuries sustained by the petitioner.,
Hence out of Rs.11,07,579/- sum of Rs.1,30,560/- has to be deducted.
On such deduction the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner would come around Rs. 9,77,019/-
As such petitioner is entitled for Rs.9,77,019/- under the head medical expenses.
27. It is stated that petitioner was aged about 26 years.
He was working in a Zanskar Research Private Limited and he has obtained the offer letter from the above said company with a package of Rs.31,00,000/- with a bonus of Rs.4,00,000/-.

The petitioner has produced offer letter issued by the company as Ex.P16.
28.
From the evidence of PW.1 it can be gathered that as of now he is getting annual package amount of Rs.66,00,000/-.
As per the Ex.P16, at the time of his joining the service his package amount was Rs.31,00,000/-.
Hence it can be said that there is no loss of future income due to the injury sustained by the petitioner.
Hence only it appears that petitioner has not examined the Medical officer to assess his physical disability.

29. It is vehemently submitted by the learned counsel for petitioner that due to the accidental injuries there was delay of two months and 14 days in joining the service, hence there is loss of salary for a period of 2 months and it has to be compensated to the petitioner.
30. As per the Ex.P16 (ie.,) the offer letter given to the petitioner from the company, he was ordered to join the service on 17.05.2023 which shall not be later than 19.05.2023.
Admittedly accident in question was occurred on 14.05.2023.
The petitioner has sustained 4 grievous injuries and he was in the hospital for 10 days and has incurred huge medical expenses of Rs.9,77,019/-.
Hence, the possibility of his taking rest for a period of 2 months cannot be ruled out.

But for the accident if the Saswat Khuntia vs Manjunath on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30676209/
7 petitioner had joined the service on 17.05.2023 he would have get two months salary and because of his joining the service 2 months later, there is loss of salary for a period of 2 months.

sentences.text:
Hence the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,16,666/- i.e., 31,00,000/- /12 =2,58,333 x 2 =
5,16,666/-.
31.
From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment at Manipal Hospitals, Bangalore.
Further for 10 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.
He has taken nourishment and needs further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.
Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.30,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2024.
32. The petitioner has contended that he is aged about 26 years as on the date of accident.
The petitioner has produced Ex.P14/Aadhar card which shows his date of birth as 04-08-1997 that means he was aged about 27 years.
Hence considering the Aadhar card this court has taken the age of the petitioner as 27 years.
33. The petitioner at his age of 27 years has suffered grievous injuries which definitely would cause some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities in life.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs 1,50,000/- towards loss of comfort and amenities.

Thereby petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:
Sl.N Heads Amount o.
1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 80,000/-

2 . Medical expenses Rs. 9,77,019/-
3. Towards loss of income during Rs. 5,16,666/-
 laid up period 4.

Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 30,000/-
 charges and nourishing food 5. Loss of discomfort and amenities Rs. 1,50,000/-

Total Rs.17,53,685/-
Therefore, this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.17,53,685/- (Rupees Seventeen Lakhs Fifty Three Thousand Six Hundred Eighty Five only).
34. As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Since both petitioner and respondent no.2 had contributed negligence to the extent of 10:90 this court has already come to the conclusion that out of the total compensation amount, petitioner has to forgo compensation to an extent of 10%.

The respondent no 2 being the insurer is liable to pay 90% of the Saswat Khuntia vs Manjunath on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30676209/
8 awarded compensation to the petitioner.
90% of the compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
accordingly issue no 2 is answered.
35. Issue No.3:
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.17,53,685/- (Rupees Seventeen Lakh Fifty Three Thousand Six Hundred Eighty Five only).

The Respondent No 2 is liable to pay 90% of the compensation amount i.e., sum of Rs.15,78,317/-
(Rupees Fifteen Lakh Seventy Eight Thousand Three Hundred Seventeen only) with interest at 6%
within 2 months from the date of this award.
It shall also carry interest at 6% per annum on Rs.15,78,317/- from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Petitioner shall forgo 50% of the compensation amount i.e., to the extent of Rs.1,75,368/-.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

As petitioner had incurred medical expanses to the tune of Rs.9,77,019/-, considering the said fact,
on deposit of the amount and interest, 30% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 70% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.
5. Respondent no.2 /the insurer of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51/MN-1447 has filed written statement and contended that the claim petition is barred by limitation and that there is 7 days delay in lodging the complaint and that in the police complaint, FIR, Panchanama and sketch the registration number of the alleged offending vehicle is not mentioned.
opennyai_summary.issue:
6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained injuries on account of road traffic accident on 14-05-2023 at about 11-00 pm, near Vydehi Hospital road, near KTPO Junction, Bangalore, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-M-1447?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
3.
What Order or Award?
7.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On the basis of the complaint lodged by Debendra Chandra Khuntia, case has been registered against the driver of Unknown 4 wheeler in Crime No.0059/2023 of Mahadavapura Traffic Police Station for the offence punishable under section 283, 337 of IPC and U/sec.134(a&b), 187 of MV Act.
All the family members of the petitioner are residing at Odisa.
After the accident the father of th petitioner who is a Government employee came down to Bangalore to take care of the petitioner.
Hence it is quit natural that when complainant is stranger to Bangalore and when there is no one in Bangalore to take care of the petitioner, under Such circumstances the presence of the complainant being the father of the petitioner is required in the hospital.
If the medical records are perused, soon after the accident the petitioner was shifted to the Manipal Hospital wherein MLC was registered and police intimation was sent, to the jurisdictional police station which is evident from Ex.P18 and 19.
When police intimation was sent it is the duty of the Jurisdictional PS to visit the hospital and to record the statement of the injured, if injured was in a position to give statement or else the statement of the attendant.
Hence for the fault of the jurisdictional police the petitioner canot be blamed.
In a judgment given in MFA No.399/2012 (MV)
between united India Insurance Company Ltd VS Smt. SK Saroja and Another decided on 21.06.2019 by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
Saswat Khuntia vs Manjunath on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30676209/
4 15.
In the light of the observation made in the aforesaid judgment coupled with the fact that MLC was registered and MLC report was given to the jurisdictional police and the fact that petitioner is the resident of Odisa and petitioner has sustained grievous and injury and was in the hospital from the date of accident till 24.05.2023, it can be said that the petitioner has assigned valid reason for delay in lodging the complaint.
Hence the delay of 7 days in lodging the complaint will not go to the root of the case of the complainant.
The driver of the offending vehicle has given confessional statement on 21.07.2023.
The vehicle was inspected through RTO on 23.06.2023.
Hence within a period of 1 month and 9 days from the date of accident the possibility of repairing the damage caused to the offending vehicle cannot be ruled out.
In MFA No. 21668/2009 c/w MFA No.22583/2009 between the Divisional Manager National Insurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Savitri and others decided on 03.09.2012 by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
Admittedly the petitioner and driver of the offending vehicle have admitted their guilty before the jurisdictional magistrate and deposited the fine amount.
If the charge sheet is perused, at the time of accident the offending vehicle came from Vaidehi hospital towards Grafite India Juction in a rash and negligent manner and without giving any indication all of a sudden took the vehicle towards KTPO by taking right turn and hit to the vehicle of the petitioner which was proceeding from Grafite India Junction towards Vaidehi hospital.
If the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, the petitioner was proceeding in the straight road and the offending vehicle by taking right U turn hit to the motor cycle of the petitioner.
Hence the offending vehicle while taking U turn and while entering the main door ought to have taken all care and caution.
Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken, this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.80,000/- towards pain and suffering.
Further the driver of offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.
opennyai_summary.arguments: It is submitted by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 that since respondent no.2 is not a party to the charge sheet, they cannot question the charge sheet.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Thereby petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:
Sl.N Heads Amount o.
1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 80,000/-
2 . Medical expenses Rs. 9,77,019/-
3. Towards loss of income during Rs. 5,16,666/-
 laid up period 4.
Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 30,000/-
 charges and nourishing food 5. Loss of discomfort and amenities Rs. 1,50,000/-
Total Rs.17,53,685/-
Therefore, this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.17,53,685/- (Rupees Seventeen Lakhs Fifty Three Thousand Six Hundred Eighty Five only).
Since both petitioner and respondent no.2 had contributed negligence to the extent of 10:90 this court has already come to the conclusion that out of the total compensation amount, petitioner has to forgo compensation to an extent of 10%.
The respondent no 2 being the insurer is liable to pay 90% of the Saswat Khuntia vs Manjunath on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30676209/
8 awarded compensation to the petitioner.
90% of the compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
accordingly issue no 2 is answered.
35. Issue No.3:
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.17,53,685/- (Rupees Seventeen Lakh Fifty Three Thousand Six Hundred Eighty Five only).
The Respondent No 2 is liable to pay 90% of the compensation amount i.e., sum of Rs.15,78,317/-
(Rupees Fifteen Lakh Seventy Eight Thousand Three Hundred Seventeen only) with interest at 6%
within 2 months from the date of this award.
It shall also carry interest at 6% per annum on Rs.15,78,317/- from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Petitioner shall forgo 50% of the compensation amount i.e., to the extent of Rs.1,75,368/-.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.
As petitioner had incurred medical expanses to the tune of Rs.9,77,019/-, considering the said fact,
on deposit of the amount and interest, 30% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 70% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
